title: Introductions; hospital work; family portraits
description: The interviewer and Myrtle exchange pleasantries about mutual acquaintances at the hospital. Myrtle shows an 1815 painted portrait of Sam Cordis, explaining how such paintings represented home wherever her family lived, and worries about who will care for it after she is gone.

title: The miner's book; meeting Harry
description: Myrtle shows an old underlined book given to her mother by a cultured miner on the Clearwater River. She then tells how she met her husband Harry Warren when he came to her house at noon as a young schoolteacher, despite her parents preferring a wealthier suitor.

title: Mountain life; losing a child; school consolidation
description: She describes living on remote Bear Ridge, losing a baby when the doctor could not reach them through deep snow, and their subsequent moves to Moscow and Kamiah as Harry taught and consolidated schools changed rural education.

title: Literary societies; childhood chores
description: Myrtle recalls the Literary Society programs, dialogues, and Christmas performances that entertained communities before radio. She describes sharing farm chores with her brother and learning practical skills from her parents.

title: Learning from parents; gardening
description: She explains how her parents taught her to identify plants and work the soil, skills she used when visiting Glacier Park. She describes raising hundreds of plants carefully with special gravel and sawdust.

title: Depression living; quilting and needlework
description: Myrtle recounts raising chickens and gardens during the Depression to keep grocery bills low. She demonstrates her quilts made from old clothing, her knitting, crocheting, and embroidery, including a memory quilt charting all the places she lived.

title: Television and reading; ice cream days
description: She discusses watching wildlife shows and "The Waltons," reading Carla Emery's country living book and historical recipe collections. She describes cutting river ice for their ice house and making homemade ice cream.

title: Volunteer work; paying off the house
description: Since her husband died, Myrtle volunteers at the hospital, museum, and senior center, visiting depressed elderly people. She reflects on working at the hospital to pay off their Lewiston house so they could retire securely.
